review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the main candidates for repeated proofs. The file's own duplicate pairs are short: span_range_list_get is the f = id case of span_range_map_list_get, and the two ideal_quotient_length_le_of_bound calls are one-liners. I judged those too small to report. I then grepped the repository for the Artinian-quotient / finite-length argument in finiteLength_localized_minimal_quotient and found it repeated in other files. The one finding is that block. I did not verify the full transitive import graph. The lemma local_quotient_length_ne_top_of_radical lives in InvariantDerivationLemmas, which I could not confirm is already imported by this file's dependencies. So the proposal is to move the shared lemma into a lower-level file, not to call it in place. I did not check whether such a move would create an import cycle. Nothing was compiled.

findings.problem: The proof first shows J.radical = maximalIdeal L. It then redoes, inline, the generic argument that a local Noetherian quotient with radical equal to the maximal ideal is Artinian and has finite length. That argument rebuilds minimal-prime membership, derives IsArtinianRing, transfers it to IsArtinian over the ring via the surjective algebraMap, and applies Module.length_ne_top. The same reasoning is already proved in InvariantDerivationLemmas as local_quotient_artinian_of_radical and local_quotient_length_ne_top_of_radical. Two more copies carry the same Artinian-quotient / length ≠ ⊤ proof: Lech.Primary.artinian_quotient and the NormalizationPresentationLocalEquiv lemma component_local_length_ne_top. A byte-for-byte copy of this whole theorem also sits in PiExponent/LocalAlgebra/AffineLocalRegularBezout.lean. So the same non-trivial commutative-algebra step is maintained in at least five places.
findings.proposed_change:
Put one general lemma in a low-level shared file that this file already imports:

theorem local_quotient_length_ne_top_of_radical {R} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (J : Ideal R) (hJ : J.radical = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) : Module.length R (R ⧸ J) ≠ ⊤.

The existing InvariantDerivationLemmas version already has this statement and proof: rewrite the minimal primes of J via Ideal.radical_minimalPrimes, apply IsLocalRing.quotient_artinian_of_mem_minimalPrimes_of_isLocalRing, use isArtinian_of_surjective_algebraMap, then Module.length_ne_top.

Then rewrite the target lemma as:
  have hrad := localized_radical_eq_maximal_of_mem_minimalPrimes I P hP
  exact Module.length_ne_top_iff.mp (local_quotient_length_ne_top_of_radical _ hrad)
The hypotheses are the same: R is Noetherian and P is prime, so Localization.AtPrime P is local and Noetherian by instance.

This removes the J.radical.IsPrime and hmin bookkeeping, which is the unneeded detour through minimalPrimes. The pi-exponent copy and the Lech.Primary / component_local_* variants can call the same lemma.
findings.benefit: The Artinian-and-finite-length argument would be stated and proved once. The target theorem would shrink from about 19 lines to 2–3. Later fixes, such as an API change to IsLocalRing.quotient_artinian_of_mem_minimalPrimes_of_isLocalRing, would touch one place instead of at least five.
